reports.title: Ross Stores Reports Strong Third Quarter Sales and Earnings Results

guidance.heading: Fiscal 2026 Guidance
section: Mr. Conroy commented, “Looking ahead to the holiday season, we are excited about the opportunities in front of us and confident in the plans we have in place for the remainder of the year. For the fourth quarter, we are maintaining our outlook for comparable store sales growth of 4% to 5%, on top of last year’s strong 9% gain. Earnings per share are expected to be in the range of $2.16 to $2.25 or growth of 8% to 13%.”

Mr. Conroy continued, “Based on our year-to-date results and our updated fourth quarter guidance, we are increasing our 2026 fiscal year earnings per share projections to be in the range of $8.75 to $8.84. As a reminder, our full year guidance includes an approximate $0.60 earnings per share benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds recognized in the second quarter.”

Mr. Conroy concluded, “The market share gains we have achieved reinforce our confidence in the opportunities ahead, and we believe we are well positioned to continue strengthening our competitive position and driving sustainable, profitable growth over the long term.”

The Company will host a conference call on Thursday, November 19, 2026 at 4:15 p.m. Eastern time to provide additional details concerning its third quarter results and management’s outlook for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 2026. A real-time audio webcast of the conference call will be available in the Investors section of the Company’s website, located at www.rossstores.com. An audio playback will be available at 201-612-7415, PIN #13763498 until 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on November 27, 2026, as well as on the Company’s website.

desk.headline: Sales up 12% to $6.26bn, in line; EPS $1.91 beats; full-year EPS outlook raised, Q4 range nudged down

other.label: Comparable store sales
other.change: on top of +7% a year ago

results: Sales rose 12% to $6.26bn and comparable store sales grew 8%, mostly from more customer visits.
Operating margin widened by 0.7 points to 12.3%, ahead of the company's own 11.7%-12.0% plan.
EPS of $1.91 (up from $1.58) beat both the company's $1.75-$1.83 guidance and the analyst estimate.
51 new stores opened in the quarter, completing the 115-store plan for 2026.
Ross bought back $319m of shares in the quarter, remains on track for $1.275bn this year, and kept its quarterly dividend at $0.445.

guidance.summary: Full-year EPS guidance went up to $8.75-$8.84 (from $8.61-$8.77), helped by the third-quarter beat; this includes about $0.60 from tariff refunds booked in Q2. Q4 comparable sales growth was kept at 4%-5%, but the Q4 EPS range slipped by one cent at each end, mainly on higher fuel costs.

points: Management credited traffic - new, returning and more frequent shoppers - for most of the sales growth.
Unusually warm weather hurt fall clothing late in the quarter, and consumer confidence was described as very weak.
Ross said it will not raise prices to chase short-term sales, to protect its value image.
Holiday was described as off to a solid start, with some extra spending on marketing and store staff; higher freight and fuel costs weigh on Q4.
Management kept its long-term model of store growth, 3%-4% comparable sales and double-digit EPS growth, but gave no 2027 outlook.
call.source: Investing.com call transcript summary, 19 Nov 2026; Panabee results note, 19 Nov 2026 (prior guidance ranges)

watch: Whether Q4 comparable sales reach 4%-5% against last year's 9% gain.
Fuel and freight costs, which the company flagged as a Q4 margin headwind.
The first fiscal 2027 outlook, due with the Q4 results.
